newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's July industrial output soars 17.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's July industrial output soars 17.1 pct.

text.p: Mexico's Finance Ministry said Sunday that industrial production in July rose 17.1 percent compared to the same month a year earlier.
The ministry said it was the sixth consecutive month of positive growth.

The ministry said industrial production was up a total of 8.0 percent for the first seven months of the year. It said year-year growth was 4.1 percent in February, 2.8 percent in March, 8.3 percent in April, 13.2 percent in May, and 12.0 percent in June.

Breaking down the industrial output in sectors, the ministry said mining activity was up 5.7 percent in July over July last year and over the first seven months it recorded a positive growth of 6.7 percent compared to the same period a year earlier. "This result is due to the favorable output from petroleum and non-petroleum mining sectors," it said.
The generation of gas, electricity and water was up 5.9 percent in July compared to July 1995 and in the first seven months was higher 3.9 percent against the same period a year earlier.
Manufacturing grew a year-on-year 18.1 percent in July and was up 9.5 percent between January and July against the first seven months of 1995.
Construction soared 22.6 percent in July over the seventh month of 1995 and was up 3.2 percent between January and July against the same period a year earlier.

The ministry said the July construction output was the third consecutive positive monthly figure and that the 22.6 percent figure was the result of "low levels of activity that the sector recorded last (1995) July."
